problem: Both bonuses are advertised as real, but the printed text says the opposite for every wearer the app can actually model: 'While you remain loyal to another deity, you BELIEVE the cassock grants you a +2 item bonus to Religion checks and a +1 item bonus to the divine skill... It does NEITHER. The GM secretly adjusts your checks with those skills, causing you to fail at religious tasks more often.' The app has no way to know the cassock's secret true unholy deity, so the authored condition can never resolve true, and the sheet will show a star promising +2 Religion to a character who has no bonus at all. The entry also omits the load-bearing negation clause ('If you have multiple equal or lower item bonuses to the affected skills, the cassock takes precedence, negating those bonuses') -- so it surfaces only the half of the rule that helps. Secondary: the second bonus uses targets skill/'all', which stars EVERY skill on the sheet for a bonus that only one deity-specific skill would ever get.
correction: drop

problem: The two situational clauses are mechanically correct (Lastwall Soup, equipment-516, grants '+2 item bonus to Stealth checks and DCs against undead' for 1 hour, so the improved/greater versions scale that to +3/+4; the 10 temporary HP for 10 minutes is printed). But the `quote` field is NOT the printed text — the feat says 'At 10th level, you can make an improved version of Lastwall soup that grants a +3 item bonus. At 18th level, you can make a greater version of Lastwall soup that grants a +4 item bonus...'. The strings 'Lastwall Soup (Improved)' and 'Lastwall Soup (Greater)' appear nowhere in feat-3614.
correction: Keep BOTH situational clauses exactly as authored — they are correct. Only replace the quote with the verbatim sentence: 'At 10th level, you can make an improved version of Lastwall soup that grants a +3 item bonus. At 18th level, you can make a greater version of Lastwall soup that grants a +4 item bonus, and its nourishing properties grant you 10 temporary Hit Points that last up to 10 minutes after eating it.'

problem: Third clause is wrong: it hangs a '+14 status' off a `classDc` target. The printed text says two separate things — 'the Dragon Breath action uses your class DC' (no numeric bonus at all) and, at 18th level, 'you gain a +14 status bonus to your Dragon Breath damage'. The +14 is a DAMAGE bonus, not a bonus to your class DC. As authored, a reader of the Class DC stat sees '+14 status' and will believe their class DC is +14, which is a bonus that does not exist. The first two clauses (+20-foot status fly Speed, dragon Strike damage bonus to +12, both at 18th) are correct.
correction: Split the third clause in two. (a) targets classDc, when: 'on the Dragon Breath action while you're transformed by Dragon Transformation', bonus: 'the DC is your class DC' — no numeric value. (b) targets strikeDamage (or a damage/note target), when: 'on Dragon Breath damage while transformed, from 18th level', bonus: '+14 status'. Do not leave any numeric bonus attached to classDc.

problem: Bonus TYPE is not confirmed by the record's own printed text. The work-file record (and the legacy printing, AoN equipment-406 'Horseshoes of Speed', CRB pg. 604) both say '+3 item bonus to Athletics checks'; only the remastered AoN record (equipment-3013, GM Core pg. 272) says '+2 circumstance bonus' (greater: '+3'). Authoring '+3 circumstance' makes the star contradict the description shown next to it in the app. (Target is fine: CompanionsTab.tsx:461-468 surfaces FEAT_SITUATIONAL[inv.itemId] on the companion block, so an animal-companion Athletics bonus does have a display surface, matching the existing 'steadyfoot-tassel' precedent.)
correction: +3 item — match the record's own text; if the GM Core remaster wording is preferred instead, fix the record's description to say 'circumstance' first so the two agree

problem: Rules content is right (+1/+2/+3/+4 item on the ongoing Fortitude save vs the drug's addiction), but the entry is filed on a record no character can ever hold. `addiction-suppressant` is an unpriced family head with 4 kin, so findUmbrellaIds() (src/data/index.ts) hides it from every item list — characterSituationalIds() only walks inventory, so this star can never fire. Worse, `situational` is in UMBRELLA_MECHANICAL_FIELDS, so writing this field onto the record un-hides it and re-adds a priceless duplicate to the shop (Ruling A regression).
correction: Move to the four priced variants: addiction-suppressant-lesser (+1 item), -moderate (+2), -greater (+3), -major (+4), each on Fortitude vs the ongoing addiction save of the drug it was crafted for. Drop the parent.
